topology: Complement-symmetric NAE encoding, equality copies, constrained entropy reservoir, injective exact residual transfer.
adversarial: Model multiplicity must include auxiliary and reservoir bits.
Balance does not mean independence, and high entropy rate does not mean inverse-polynomial density.
Copies and redundant syntactic links do not imply a computationally irreducible core.
K may exceed k; conditional hardness does not prove P!=NP.

cost: h=2(n+1+8 binom(n,3))+1+(n+2)^a for fixed a epsilon>3; polynomial full selector generation, exact fixed target stage and projection; fixed source exponent absorbed into K.

planner.question: Does high model entropy combined with balanced variables, essential bits and syntactic connectivity force tractability, or can arbitrary original SAT residuals transfer into that class?
planner.strategy: Encode arbitrary source SAT with globally complement-symmetric NAE constraints, enforce essential copy pairs, attach a high-entropy constrained reservoir and charge original stage transfer.
planner.alternative: Derive conditional unrestricted equivalence within the high-entropy class and explicitly distinguish density, marginal balance and syntactic connectivity.
planner.stop_rule: No unconditional hardness claim, no inverse-polynomial density guarantee, no same-exponent transfer.
literature_leads: Elementary NAE split gadget, complement symmetry and padding; prior F038 few-model isolation and exact U residual transfer. No novelty claim.

construct.claim: For any fixed rational epsilon>0, a polynomial injection maps all satisfiable original selectors eventually to complement-symmetric connected targets with at least 2^(h-h^epsilon) models and every variable semantically essential.
construct.scope: Original full normalized selectors, exact same U, fixed rational epsilon>0 and fixed k, eventual residual injection from some K>=k; entropy rate not inverse-polynomial density.
construct.derivation: Reference-bit interpretation, NAE split, dedicated auxiliaries, copy equality and redundant syntactic links, exact reservoir size and model count; injective clause markers.
unresolved_steps: Unbounded cubic-stage failure or uniform SAT cutoff.
candidate_tests: Exhaust small source/base/reservoir assignments, actual selector marker recovery, complement balance and essential flips.

alternative.claim: For each k,epsilon some K>=k transfers B_K(n) into high-entropy B_k(h) for all sufficiently large n; all-exponent hardness on that class is equivalent to P!=NP.
alternative.scope: Original full normalized selectors, exact same U, fixed rational epsilon>0 and fixed k, eventual residual injection from some K>=k; entropy rate not inverse-polynomial density.
alternative.derivation: Fixed polynomial constructor plus actual target stage and verified projection; absorb description and time in K, apply prior unrestricted equivalence.
unresolved_steps: Numerical K and unconditional unbounded source hardness.
No inverse polynomial assignment density theorem.
candidate_tests: Check exact model-count factor and target length, full original verifier and graph connectivity.

objections: Model multiplicity must include auxiliary and reservoir bits.
Balance does not mean independence, and high entropy rate does not mean inverse-polynomial density.
Copies and redundant syntactic links do not imply a computationally irreducible core.
K may exceed k; conditional hardness does not prove P!=NP.
counterexample_candidates: The reservoir is easy to fill and hardness lives in source projection.
Unsatisfiable targets have no balanced model distribution; the balance property is asserted only for SAT.
